question.text: Consider the system of equations <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>∈</mo><mfenced open="{" close="}" separators="|"><mrow><mn>0,1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3,4</mn></mrow></mfenced><mo>.</mo></math> The number of ordered pairs <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"></mi><mi>b</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> for which the system has non-trivial solutions is

solution.text:
For non-trivial solutions,
a1bb1aabab=0
⇒a-ba-b2=0
⇒ Either a=b or a=b2
When a=b, then ordered pairs are 0,0,1,1,2,2,3,3,4,4
When a=b2, then 4,2
Hence, number of ordered pairs are 6
